title: One MU mark, one failed run, and no recorded fills
body_html:
One MU mark, one failed run, and no recorded fills

Paper trading · 2026-10-27T17:00:14.801134-04:00

This report uses records through 2026-10-27 21:00:14 UTC. The paper account snapshot at that time shows $2,000 cash and equity. The mean-reversion book has one listed MU holding and a cutoff mark just below its $2,000 starting cash; the other two books show $2,000 cash and equity. A scheduled run failed at 19:16:13 UTC because the research planner context exceeded its configured limit. That failure is not a deliberate wait or a completed decision. The supplied context contains no order lifecycle records, deterministic risk approvals or rejections, or broker or simulated fills. The MU quote was observed at 20:00:00 UTC and is a last-session observation, not a live price.

Today's lesson: A snapshot is a timestamped estimate

A recorded midpoint is an estimate, not a guaranteed closing or live price. Here, the midpoint of the $874.00 bid and $967.56 ask is ($874.00 + $967.56) ÷ 2 = $920.78. Applied to 0.053191 shares, that gives a marked value of about $48.98. The observation was timestamped 20:00:00 UTC, one hour before the report cutoff, and the book’s $1.0159 unrealized loss excludes fees.

What the records can and cannot show

A submitted order would not by itself prove a fill, and broker fills and simulated book fills are separate records. Here, neither kind of fill is supplied. The failed run also does not establish that a trade was proposed or rejected.

What to watch next

Check whether later records contain a completed run, a proposed order and its deterministic risk result, and any broker or simulated fills. Compare each price observation’s timestamp with the activity it is being used to describe.

Bid/ask midpoint: A price estimate made by averaging the recorded bid and ask. It can differ from an executable trade price.

Unrealized P/L: The gain or loss on a holding that has not been sold, based here on the recorded observation price and book purchase basis.

Realized P/L: Gain or loss recorded from completed sales. The mean-reversion book reports $0 realized P/L at the cutoff.

Data timing and limitations

Prices come from recorded snapshots, not a guaranteed closing-price feed.
Paper account holdings use the latest recorded snapshot, which may precede fills.
Book marks use observed bid/ask midpoints at price_as_of, not guaranteed live prices. Without an admitted quote the value remains unknown; book gains exclude fees.
Work starting after the cutoff is outside this report. Failures remain labelled.
